caption:
Pattern of life is built from repeated passes, not one look. A single image shows a moment. Only a sequence — the same area, revisited over days or weeks — shows what is normal there, so an analyst can flag what is not.

The honest limit: between passes, the area is dark. If something starts and finishes inside that gap, the pattern never registers it. Revisit interval sets the floor on what pattern-of-life analysis can actually see — no amount of sharpening the image afterward fixes that.

This is why collection plans fix cadence before an incident, not after. You cannot backfill a pattern you never sampled.

card.headline: A pattern needs more than one pass
card.sub: Repeated revisits establish what's normal. Anything that starts and ends between passes never enters the record.

rationale: Introduces a distinct capability (pattern-of-life analysis) with its own honest limit (the inter-pass gap), without repeating prior cadence/silence framings.
